attrs.evidence: governance/blind_package.mjs; blind-package.json; `--emit` copies exactly the manifested bytes so the clean room mounts the thing that was measured. TWO DRAFTS OF THE EXCLUSION CHECK WERE WRONG AND BOTH FAILED LOUDLY: a substring blocklist on `holdout` flagged holdout_score_core.mjs and holdout_schema.mjs, which ARE the frozen instrument and belong in the package; a search for the type token TRVM-PROOF-WIRE-HOLDOUT-v2 then flagged the two documents that DEFINE the challenge type. A name cannot tell the scorer from the challenges it scores. Negative arm measured: copying a hidden challenge into vectors/public/ under an innocuous name is caught twice, by digest and by shape. Gate `gov-spec` and `gov-nest`; grid boolean blind-package-bound.
attrs.statement: A SEMANTIC IDENTITY IS NOT AN ARTIFACT IDENTITY, AND THE CLEAN ROOM RECEIVES BYTES. `srel` identifies what the specification MEANS; it does not identify what was DELIVERED. MEASURED: BLIND-IMPLEMENTATION-CONTRACT section 2 hands the implementer docs/spec/proof-wire/requirements/open/, which spec_release.mjs excludes from spec_digest BY CONSTRUCTION because a declared-open register must be free to grow -- so editing RFC8785-number-stress-corpus.md left SPEC-RELEASE and BLIND-RUN passing with identical identities while changing a document the blind implementer reads. The repair is NOT to fold requirements/ into spec_digest, which would make a declared-open register into normative text; it is `bpkg-H(manifest)` over every byte under the package root, the same split as verified_claim_sem_id versus artifact_root. A run pins BOTH. AND THE EXCLUSIONS ARE PROVEN RATHER THAN PROMISED: the hidden challenge set is excluded BY DIGEST and by H*-id shape, not by name.
